guides.one_liner: Emaar's city centre around Burj Khalifa and The Dubai Mall, with high-rise apartments, a busy boulevard and Metro access, where most of today's sales are ready homes.
guides.what_it_is: Downtown Dubai is Emaar's master-planned centre, set between Sheikh Zayed Road and Financial Centre Road. It is built around its landmarks: Burj Khalifa, The Dubai Mall and The Dubai Fountain, with Dubai Opera close by. Homes are mostly apartments in towers along Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Boulevard and the Opera District. It is dense, walkable at its core and busy with visitors most of the year, so it feels like a city centre more than a residential suburb.
guides.who_buys: Investors looking for rental demand in a central address, and professionals who want to live near work, the mall and the Metro. Overseas buyers often treat it as a first Dubai purchase because the landmarks are known worldwide. Families buy here less than in villa communities. Short-stay landlords are active because of the visitor traffic.
things_to_consider: Burj Khalifa / Dubai Mall Metro station serves the area, but traffic around the mall is heavy at peak times and during events.
Service charges vary by building. Check the RERA-approved rate in DLD's Service Charge Index before you commit.
Short-stay letting needs a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism.
Visitor numbers bring noise and crowds near the Boulevard and the Fountain.
guides.my_view: Sales here fell much faster than the Dubai market in the first half, then slightly less than the market in the third quarter. Most deals are ready homes, not off-plan, so prices reflect what buyers pay for finished units today. That gives plenty of real transactions to test any asking price against.

guides.one_liner: Emaar's waterfront district of towers around a man-made marina, with a promenade, tram stops and a mature resale market where most sales are ready homes.
guides.what_it_is: Dubai Marina is one of Emaar's earliest waterfront master plans, built around a man-made marina with towers on both sides. Life centres on Dubai Marina Walk, a waterfront promenade lined with cafés and restaurants, along with Dubai Marina Mall, Pier 7 and the Dubai Marina Yacht Club. Dubai Tram stops run through the district. It is one of the areas Dubai's freehold regulation names for ownership by non-nationals.
guides.who_buys: Investors after rental demand from young professionals, and end users who want waterfront living with transport close by. It draws a large share of overseas buyers and short-stay landlords. Families who need more space usually look at villa communities instead.
things_to_consider: It is a mature area, so building age and upkeep vary. Check each tower's maintenance record and its RERA-approved service charge.
Short-stay letting needs a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism.
Roads around the Marina get congested at peak times. Dubai Tram stops serve the district.
Few new launches here, so value depends on resale demand.
guides.my_view: Sales have fallen further than the Dubai average this year, in both the first half and the third quarter. The great majority of deals are ready homes in an established district, so the slowdown here is resale demand, not a gap in new launches. In a mature area like this, price evidence comes from real resales, and right now there are fewer of them.

guides.one_liner: Emaar and Meraas's green master plan around a championship golf course and Dubai Hills Park, with villas, townhouses and apartments in a family-led community.
guides.what_it_is: Dubai Hills Estate is a joint venture between Emaar and Meraas within Mohammed bin Rashid City, with road access from Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Street. Emaar calls it "the green heart of Dubai". It is built around a championship golf course and Dubai Hills Park, with Dubai Hills Mall as its retail centre. Housing ranges from villas and townhouses on landscaped streets to apartment buildings near the mall and the park.
guides.who_buys: Mainly families buying villas and townhouses to live in, plus investors buying apartments near the mall and the park for rental demand. Many buyers move here from other parts of Dubai for more space and greenery. Overseas buyers are active in the apartment segment.
things_to_consider: Access is mainly by road from Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Street, so check your commute at peak hours.
Villas and apartments behave like different markets here. Compare like with like.
Service charges differ between villa communities and apartment buildings. Check the RERA-approved rates.
Some phases are still being built, so expect construction nearby in newer parts.
guides.my_view: Dubai Hills moved roughly in line with the Dubai market in the first half, then fell harder than the market in the third quarter. Sales are split between ready homes and off-plan, with ready homes the larger share lately. A swing that sharp means the recent pace of sales alone isn't a reliable guide here, so I would look at deals for the specific home type, not the area average.

guides.one_liner: Emaar's waterfront district on Dubai Creek beside Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary, close to Downtown and the airport, where most sales are off-plan and phases are still rising.
guides.what_it_is: Dubai Creek Harbour is an Emaar master plan on the Dubai Creek shoreline, next to the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary, a protected wetland known for its flamingos. Emaar places it a short drive from Downtown Dubai and Dubai International Airport. It is a mixed-use waterfront district of residential towers, offices and shops, with the Creek Beach promenade as a public focus. Much of it is still being built in phases.
guides.who_buys: Investors buying off-plan on payment plans, and end users who want a waterfront home near the city centre and the airport. It draws overseas buyers looking for a newer district at an earlier stage. Families buy here, though the area is mostly apartments.
things_to_consider: Most current sales are off-plan, so check each project's escrow account, registration and payment plan against construction progress.
A Dubai Metro Blue Line station is planned for the area. Until it opens, access is by road.
Construction will continue around finished buildings for some time.
Check the expected service charge for each building against DLD's Service Charge Index.
guides.my_view: This is one of the few guide areas that grew in the first half, and its third-quarter fall was much smaller than Dubai's as a whole. Most deals are off-plan, so the figures reflect developer launches as much as resale demand. Read its resilience with that in mind.

guides.one_liner: Nakheel's island master plan off Dubai's northern coast near the airport, with beaches, resorts and marinas planned, where every recorded sale this year has been off-plan.
guides.what_it_is: Dubai Islands, formerly known as Deira Islands, is a Nakheel master plan of man-made islands off Dubai's northern coastline, a short distance from Dubai International Airport. The plan centres on beaches, including a Blue Flag certified beach, resorts and hotels, marinas and golf. Bridges will connect the islands to the mainland via the Al Shindagha Corridor. Infrastructure contracts are still being awarded, so this is an area in the early stage of development.
guides.who_buys: Mostly investors buying off-plan on payment plans, attracted by beachfront positioning close to the airport and old Dubai. Overseas buyers are prominent. End users are fewer for now, because most homes are not yet built. Once homes are delivered, the buyer mix will be easier to read from resale activity.
things_to_consider: Every recorded sale this year has been off-plan. Check each project's escrow account, registration and payment plan.
Large parts of the master plan, including island infrastructure and bridge links, are still under construction.
Confirm the ownership terms for the specific plot with DLD before committing.
With no resale history yet, there is little transaction evidence to test prices against.
guides.my_view: Every recorded sale here this year has been off-plan. Strong growth in the first half gave way to a third-quarter fall in line with the wider Dubai market. With no resale record yet, launch pricing is the only benchmark, and that is the main pricing risk.

guides.one_liner: Nakheel's palm-shaped island of beachfront villas, apartments and resort hotels, linked by monorail and tram, and one of Dubai's most resilient areas by sales this year.
guides.what_it_is: Palm Jumeirah is Nakheel's palm-shaped island off the Jumeirah coast, made up of the trunk, the fronds and the crescent. Apartments line the trunk, villas with private beaches sit on the fronds, and resort hotels occupy the crescent. Nakheel Mall, The View at The Palm and Al Ittihad Park sit at its centre. The Palm Monorail runs along the island, and a tunnel links the trunk to the crescent. It is one of the areas Dubai's freehold regulation names for ownership by non-nationals.
guides.who_buys: High-net-worth end users buying frond villas, investors in trunk apartments for rental and short-stay demand, and overseas buyers who want a globally recognised address. Many second-home owners use the island part of the year. Villa and apartment buyers here rarely compete for the same homes.
things_to_consider: Older buildings and newer launches differ widely in specification and service charges. Check the RERA-approved rate for each building.
Short-stay letting needs a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism.
Frond villas and trunk apartments are separate markets with different buyers.
guides.my_view: Palm Jumeirah has held up better than Dubai as a whole in both the first half and the third quarter. Most deals are ready homes rather than off-plan. In a cooling market, that resilience is the main thing the data shows.

guides.one_liner: Nakheel's second palm island on Dubai's southern coast, much larger than Palm Jumeirah, now under construction, where every sale so far has been off-plan.
guides.what_it_is: Palm Jebel Ali is Nakheel's second palm island, part of a new growth corridor in the Jebel Ali area on Dubai's southern coastline. Nakheel's revised master plan makes it much larger than Palm Jumeirah, built around beachside living with a large number of hotels and resorts. Villa construction contracts have been awarded and building is under way. Dubai's freehold regulation names it for ownership by non-nationals.
guides.who_buys: Investors and end users buying off-plan villas on payment plans, many of them buyers who know Palm Jumeirah and want a similar address at an earlier stage. Overseas buyers are prominent. There are no completed homes yet, so there are no resident communities or resale buyers.
things_to_consider: Everything is off-plan. Check the escrow account, registration and payment plan against construction milestones.
Handover is still some way off, so your money is tied up before any rental income.
It is far from central Dubai, so check commute times to where you work.
With no completed homes, there is no resale market yet to test prices against.
guides.my_view: Every sale here is off-plan, with no record from last year to compare against. Third-quarter sales were higher than the whole first half while the Dubai market was falling, which is demand driven by launches, not resale. Until homes are delivered, there is no resale market to test prices against.

guides.one_liner: A government-backed maritime peninsula next to Mina Rashid, mixing maritime business, homes and leisure, where nearly all recent sales have been off-plan.
guides.what_it_is: Dubai Maritime City is a man-made peninsula next to the Mina Rashid area. It was created by Dubai law as a purpose-built maritime centre, and is now overseen by the Dubai Maritime Authority. It is a mixed-use district combining maritime industry and offices with residential and leisure space. Infrastructure for its residential and commercial phases has been laid so that sub-developers can build, and much of the housing is still new or under construction.
guides.who_buys: Mostly investors buying off-plan apartments on payment plans, drawn by waterfront positioning close to old Dubai and the Mina Rashid area. Some buyers work in maritime and port businesses nearby. Families are fewer for now, because the residential side of the district is still filling in around them.
things_to_consider: Nearly all recent sales are off-plan. Check each project's escrow account, registration and payment plan.
It is a working maritime district, so expect industrial and port activity nearby.
Confirm the ownership terms for the specific plot with DLD before committing.
Much of the area is still being built, so services and retail are still filling in.
guides.my_view: Sales have dropped sharply this year, and the third-quarter fall is the steepest of the areas I track. Nearly all deals are off-plan, so activity depends on new launches. That dependence is the first thing to weigh here.

guides.one_liner: Modon's sport and leisure island off Abu Dhabi's southwest coast, open to all nationalities, and the emirate's biggest area by sales value in the first half.
guides.what_it_is: Hudayriyat Island sits just off the southwest coast of Abu Dhabi city, opposite Al Bateen, and is linked to the mainland by the Hudayriyat Bridge. Modon is planning and developing it as a destination for sport, wellness and outdoor living. Its anchors include Surf Abu Dhabi, Velodrome Abu Dhabi, the Marsana waterfront, Circuit X, public beaches and a long cycling network. Homes range from completed communities to plots and villas still being built.
guides.who_buys: Families and end users who want an active, outdoor lifestyle close to the city, and investors buying into a master plan still in its growth stage. Modon offers freehold to all nationalities, so overseas buyers are a significant part of demand.
things_to_consider: Many homes are still under construction. Check handover timing and the payment plan against construction progress.
Construction will continue across the island for some time.
Access is by bridge from Al Bateen, so check your route to work.
Service charges in Abu Dhabi jointly owned property need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
guides.my_view: Hudayriyat led Abu Dhabi by sales value in the first half, after growing many times over on last year. That much concentration in one island, with many homes still to be handed over, means the figures reflect launches as much as settled demand. I would read the growth as momentum, not proof of resale value.

guides.one_liner: Abu Dhabi's cultural island, home to Louvre Abu Dhabi and new national museums, with beachfront communities in an investment zone and the emirate's second-largest sales value.
guides.what_it_is: Saadiyat Island is home to the Saadiyat Cultural District, which includes Louvre Abu Dhabi, Zayed National Museum, the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi and Manarat Al Saadiyat, with Guggenheim Abu Dhabi to follow. Aldar manages the island's land and is master developer of its final masterplan phase. The island combines a long natural shorefront and an ecological sand dune reserve with low-rise beachfront communities, villas and apartments, plus resort hotels.
guides.who_buys: Wealthy end users and families who want beachfront homes near the cultural district, investors seeking an established premium address, and overseas buyers. Saadiyat is an investment zone, open to foreign ownership.
things_to_consider: New phases are still being launched, so check whether a home is ready or off-plan and how long until handover.
Beachfront and conservation rules shape what can be built near the shore.
Service charges need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
Holiday home letting in Abu Dhabi needs a licence from the Department of Culture and Tourism.
guides.my_view: Saadiyat was Abu Dhabi's second-largest area by sales value in the first half and grew strongly on last year, though more slowly than the emirate as a whole. As a more established island, it offers more existing homes to compare prices with than the newest ones. Its growth rests on a wider base of finished homes than the launch-led islands.

guides.h1: Al Reem Island and Al Maryah Island
guides.one_liner: Abu Dhabi's financial district, home to ADGM, and the high-rise residential island beside it, both investment zones, with sales well ahead of last year.
guides.what_it_is: Al Maryah Island is home to Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM), the emirate's international financial centre, together with Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, The Galleria and luxury hotels. ADGM's jurisdiction extends to neighbouring Al Reem Island, a largely high-rise residential island with a central park and waterfront promenades, set between Al Maryah and Saadiyat. A Mubadala and Aldar joint venture is preparing an expansion of Al Maryah's financial district, with new bridge links planned.
guides.who_buys: Professionals working in the financial district and the city, investors buying apartments for rental demand, and overseas buyers. Both islands are investment zones open to foreign ownership. Reem has the largest stock of homes of any Abu Dhabi investment zone, which brings a wide range of buyers.
things_to_consider: Most homes are apartments in towers, and buildings vary widely in age and upkeep. Check each one.
The Al Maryah expansion means construction nearby for some time.
Service charges need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
guides.my_view: Reem and Maryah more than doubled their sales value in the first half. ADREC counts Reem as the investment zone with the most homes, so there is a deep base of existing stock. That gives more resale evidence to test prices against than the newer islands have.

guides.one_liner: Abu Dhabi's leisure island of theme parks, Yas Marina Circuit and Yas Mall, with Aldar-developed communities in an investment zone and sales well up on last year.
guides.what_it_is: Yas Island is Abu Dhabi's main leisure and entertainment destination. Its anchors include Yas Marina Circuit, home of the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, along with Ferrari World, Yas Waterworld, Warner Bros. World, SeaWorld, Etihad Arena, Yas Mall, Yas Links golf course and Yas Beach. Around these sit residential communities developed largely by Aldar, from apartments to villas and townhouses. It is an investment zone open to foreign ownership.
guides.who_buys: Families buying villas and townhouses to live in, investors buying apartments for rental demand from people working in leisure and hospitality, and overseas buyers.
things_to_consider: Major events at the circuit and arenas bring traffic and noise on event days.
New communities are still being launched alongside completed ones. Check ready versus off-plan status.
Service charges need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
Holiday home letting needs a licence from the Department of Culture and Tourism.
guides.my_view: Yas nearly doubled its sales value in the first half, a strong result though slower than Abu Dhabi's growth as a whole. As an established island with many existing communities, it has more resale evidence than the newest islands. The growth here sits on a wider base than the launch-led areas.

guides.one_liner: Eagle Hills' low-density island of bays and mangroves between Yas and Saadiyat, a newer master plan and one of Abu Dhabi's leading areas by sales value in the first half.
guides.what_it_is: Al Ramhan Island, branded Ramhan Island by its developer Eagle Hills, is a naturally formed island of bays and mangrove landscapes. It sits within a short drive of Yas Island, Saadiyat Island, Zayed International Airport and the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque. Eagle Hills plans it as a low-density community with a marina and beachfront villas, so it is quieter and more private than the busier leisure islands.
guides.who_buys: Mainly buyers of beachfront villas: end users who want a private, low-density setting close to the leisure and cultural islands, and investors buying into a newer master plan at an early stage. It suits buyers who value space and water access over walking distance to shops and restaurants.
things_to_consider: This is a newer master plan, so check handover timing and the payment plan for each phase.
Confirm investment-zone (foreign ownership) status for the specific plot with ADREC or the developer before committing.
Service charges need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
With little resale history, there is limited transaction evidence to test prices against.
guides.my_view: ADREC hasn't published a comparison with last year, so I can't say whether sales here are rising or falling. What the data does show is a place in Abu Dhabi's leading areas by value in the first half. Until there's a trend, I'd read that as one strong period, not a direction.

guides.one_liner: Aldar's wellness-led island between Yas and Saadiyat, with beachfront on one side and mangroves on the other, a recent master plan already among Abu Dhabi's leading areas.
guides.what_it_is: Al Fahid Island, now branded Fahid Island by Aldar, lies between Yas Island and Saadiyat Island beside Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Highway. Aldar acquired the island and unveiled a master plan positioning it as a wellness destination, with beachfront along one side and mangrove forests along the other. Pedestrian bridges link parts of the island internally. It is a recent launch, so homes here are off-plan.
guides.who_buys: Investors and end users buying off-plan homes in a new master plan, attracted by the wellness positioning and the location between the established leisure island of Yas and the cultural island of Saadiyat. It suits buyers prepared to wait for handover in exchange for an early position.
things_to_consider: All homes are off-plan. Check the payment plan and handover timing against construction progress.
Confirm investment-zone (foreign ownership) status with ADREC or the developer before committing.
Construction will continue across the island for years.
Service charges need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
guides.my_view: ADREC hasn't published a comparison with last year, so the direction of sales can't be read from official data yet. The island reached Abu Dhabi's leading areas by value in the first half on new launches alone. That is a measure of launch demand, not of resale value, because no homes have been delivered.

guides.one_liner: A coastal area in Ghantoot, about halfway between Abu Dhabi and Dubai, where IMKAN is building a wellness-led beachfront master plan.
guides.what_it_is: Ghadeer Al Tayr lies in Ghantoot on the Arabian Gulf coast, roughly halfway between Abu Dhabi and Dubai. Abu Dhabi's Department of Municipalities and Transport refers to it alongside Al Jurf. Developer IMKAN is building a large coastal master plan here along the shoreline, centred on beachfront homes and a wellness resort. It is far from either city centre, so it suits buyers who want space and coast over urban convenience.
guides.who_buys: Buyers who want a coastal home between Abu Dhabi and Dubai, from either emirate, and who value beach and space over city access. Second-home buyers and investors buying into a master plan at an early stage make up much of the rest.
things_to_consider: It is a long drive to central Abu Dhabi and Dubai, so check daily travel.
Much of the master plan is still being built. Check handover timing for each phase.
More than one developer may be active in the wider area. Confirm which master plan a home sits in.
Confirm investment-zone (foreign ownership) status for the specific home with ADREC or the developer before committing.
Service charges need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
guides.my_view: ADREC hasn't published a comparison with last year, so I can't say whether sales are rising or falling here. It made Abu Dhabi's leading areas by value in the first half. Until a trend is published, I'd read that as one strong period, not a proven direction.

guides.one_liner: A planned mainland district between Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Zayed International Airport, with several developers and a large share of Abu Dhabi's future home supply.
guides.what_it_is: Zayed City is a planned mainland district of Abu Dhabi, between Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Zayed International Airport, laid out under the emirate's long-term urban plan. Unlike the islands, it is a multi-developer district rather than a single master plan. It is being built out as a series of new residential communities. ADREC lists it among the few districts expected to deliver most of Abu Dhabi's new homes over the coming years.
guides.who_buys: Families and end users looking for newer mainland homes close to the airport and the existing suburbs, and investors buying into new communities at an early stage. Foreign ownership applies in designated investment-zone communities, so check each community before deciding.
things_to_consider: Ownership rules vary by community. Confirm investment-zone status for the specific home.
ADREC expects a large share of new supply here, so many competing homes will come to market.
Much of the district is still under construction.
Service charges need DMT approval. Ask for the approved rate.
guides.my_view: ADREC hasn't published a comparison with last year, so the direction of sales here isn't yet visible in official data. What ADREC does say is that Zayed City is one of the districts expected to carry much of the new supply. A lot of new homes in one area is the point to weigh first.
